name: Claros Flow
target_market: NHS acute trusts and integrated care boards
public_accuracy_claim: "94% accurate seven-day bed forecasts" (website, Oct 2026; method not published)
known_customers: 2 NHS trusts live; pilot with Pennine Vale Hospitals NHS Trust announced 14 Oct 2026
strengths: Funding; senior ex-NHS hires; polished command-centre screens
weaknesses: Single-number forecasts with no stated uncertainty; long integrations (reported 9-12 months); no published evaluation
latest_move: Press release: pilot at Pennine Vale 'live before Christmas'; says it will publish results in spring 2027

name: Oakridge Capacity Command (module of the Oakridge EPR)
target_market: Hospitals already on the Oakridge EPR
known_customers: Offered to all Oakridge EPR customers; 3 UK trusts said to be 'early adopters'
pricing_model: Bundled with EPR licence ('no additional licence cost')
strengths: Already inside the EPR; no new integration; procurement is trivial
weaknesses: Forecasting described by users as basic (rolling averages); roadmap dates slip; not available to non-Oakridge sites
latest_move: User group told a 7-day forecast is on the 2027 roadmap

name: Nationally funded data platform - patient flow tools
known_customers: Many trusts onboarded for discharge and elective tools; uptake of flow tools varies
pricing_model: No local licence cost; local implementation effort
strengths: Free to the trust; national backing; shared definitions
weaknesses: Generic; local configuration effort; trusts report mixed fit; forecasting features limited so far; contested public trust in some areas
latest_move: Programme newsletter mentions 'predictive bed demand' as a 2027 priority

name: In-house business intelligence team (spreadsheets / Power BI)
strengths: Local knowledge; no procurement; trusted by the people who built it
weaknesses: Key-person dependency; little maintenance; forecasts often abandoned after the analyst leaves

name: BedSense AI
public_accuracy_claim: "Predicts nurse demand per ward within one FTE, 85% of shifts" (case study)
strengths: Dutch and German language; integrates with the dominant Dutch EPRs; focuses on staffed beds
weaknesses: Small team; no UK presence; staffing focus rather than bed demand
latest_move: Opened a Dublin office; bidding for Irish hospital group work

name: MedOps Asia
target_market: Private hospital groups in Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam
known_customers: 5 private groups in South-East Asia (about 60 hospitals)
pricing_model: Implementation fee plus annual licence; on-site team
strengths: Local teams and language; command-centre hardware; relationships with private groups
weaknesses: Expensive for public hospitals; forecasting is rules-based; little presence in district public hospitals
latest_move: Signed a second Indonesian private group

name: Afya Insights
target_market: County health departments in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania
known_customers: Dashboards on the national health information system in 14 counties
strengths: Free; trusted by county health teams; works with monthly aggregate data; offline-tolerant
weaknesses: Monthly data only; descriptive dashboards, no forecasting; depends on grant cycles
